knowledge:
- key_parameters: filepath = path to the Seahorse XF Excel file (.xlsx) passed as the first argument to revive_xfplate()
- alternatives: None mentioned for software, but other instruments like Oroboros O2K, Hansatech oxygraphs, and Lucid Scientific ReSipher are mentioned as alternative extracellular flux analysis hardware.
- when_to_use: Use when you have raw Seahorse XF analyzer Excel output files and want to perform reproducible, standardized preprocessing, background correction, and validation of OCR and ECAR measurements.
- pitfalls: Background correction status can vary; the package automatically detects if background correction was applied by checking if background wells are zero, and applies it if missing. Users must verify the was_background_corrected attribute to ensure correct downstream interpretation.

workflows.name: seahorse_xf_preprocessing
workflows.intent: Read, preprocess, and validate Seahorse XF analyzer Excel data into structured nested tibbles.
workflows.stages: 1. Read and preprocess the Seahorse plate data using revive_xfplate(). 2. Inspect the structure of the nested tibble. 3. Extract rate data, raw data, assay information, and injection information using purrr::pluck().
workflows.code:
revive_output_donor_A <- 
  system.file("extdata", 
              "20191219_SciRep_PBMCs_donor_A.xlsx",
              package = "seahtrue") %>% 
  seahtrue::revive_xfplate()

revive_output_donor_A %>%  
  dplyr::glimpse()

revive_output_donor_A %>%  
  purrr::pluck("rate_data", 1)

revive_output_donor_A %>%  
  purrr::pluck("raw_data", 1)

revive_output_donor_A %>%  
  purrr::pluck("assay_info", 1) %>% 
  pull(cartridge_barcode)

revive_output_donor_A %>%  
  purrr::pluck("rate_data", 1) %>% 
  attributes() %>% 
  purrr::pluck("was_background_corrected")

revive_output_donor_A %>%  
  purrr::pluck("injection_info", 1)
